A '''pathogenic bomb''' was a chemical [[Missile/Legends|warhead]] that mixed two prime components together to create a [[Poison/Legends|poison]] cloud that was capable of spreading disease among targeted populations. The resulting mixture was highly volatile, which necessitated its storage in independent receptacles until just prior to deployment. In [[8 ABY/Legends|8 ABY]], the population of the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Kolatill]] in the [[Kathol sector/Legends|Kathol sector]] of the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]] was targeted by [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] [[Warlord/Legends|warlord]] [[Moff/Legends|Moff]] [[Kentor Sarne]]. The [[Battle of Kolatill|assault]] was in response to Kolatill's overthrow of their [[Tetrum|Imperial governor]] in the wake of Sarne's [[Battle of Kal'Shebbol|ousting]] from his own [[Capital/Legends|capital]], [[Kal'Shebbol/Legends|Kal'Shebbol]], by [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] [[New Republic task force (Kal'Shebbol)|forces]]. The attack&mdash;which was to feature the dropping of pathogenic bombs on major [[City/Legends|cities]] across the surface of the planet&mdash;was thwarted by the combined forces of the [[Kolatill Defense Force]] and the [[FarStar starfighter squadron|starfighter squadron]] assigned to the New Republic [[CR90 corvette/Legends|CR90 corvette]] ''[[FarStar]]''.

==Description==
Pathogenic bombs were highly toxic [[Missile/Legends|warheads]] capable of deploying a [[Poison/Legends|poison]] cloud over a vast area, spreading disease among organic populations. Such weapons comprised two prime components that, when mixed, formed a deadly poison. However, due to the volatile nature of the mixture, the two components were stored separately, and were not mixed until just prior to the bombs' release in the delivery vessel's ordnance bay. If the components remained separated, the bombs were harmless.<ref name="O" />

==History==
In [[8 ABY/Legends|8 ABY]],<ref name="Date" /> the [[Moff Sarne's forces|forces]] under the command of [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] [[Warlord/Legends|warlord]] [[Moff/Legends|Moff]] [[Kentor Sarne]] intended to deploy pathogenic bombs against the citizens of the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Kolatill]] in the [[Kathol sector/Legends|Kathol sector]] of the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]]. The [[Battle of Kolatill|assault]] was in retribution for the populace's defiance against Sarne; the populace had overthrown their local Imperial [[Governor/Legends|governor]], [[Tetrum]], and declared their allegiance to the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] when they learned that Sarne had [[Battle of Kal'Shebbol|lost control]] of his [[Capital/Legends|capital]], [[Kal'Shebbol/Legends|Kal'Shebbol]]. [[TIE/sa tactical bomber/Legends|TIE/sa bombers]] assigned to the [[Ton-Falk-class escort carrier|''Ton-Falk''-class escort carrier]] ''[[Kathol Protector]]''&mdash;which had conducted a previous [[Bombing of Domaz|assault]] on the planet four days previously&mdash;were armed with these weapons and ordered to target [[City/Legends|cities]] on Kolatill.<ref name="O" />

While the ''Kathol Protector'' and its [[TIE/ln space superiority starfighter/Legends|TIE/LN starfighters]] engaged the New Republic [[CR90 corvette/Legends|CR90 corvette]] ''[[FarStar]]''&mdash;which had arrived at the planet to render assistance to the inhabitants of the city of [[Domaz]] following the ''Kathol Protector''{{'s}} previous assault on the world&mdash;in [[Realspace/Legends|space]], TIE [[Bomber/Legends|bombers]] loaded with pathogenic bombs descended to the surface. During the resulting aerial battle between the bombers and the [[Starfighter/Legends|fighters]] of the [[Kolatill Defense Force]], alongside the [[FarStar starfighter squadron|starfighter squadron]] assigned to the ''FarStar'', one [[Pilot/Legends|pilot]] registered the presence of the pathogenic bombs aboard the bombers when one of the fighters was destroyed, and the pilot's [[Sensor/Legends|sensors]] detected poisonous chemicals in the debris field. Realizing that the bombers carried chemical weapons, the combined forces redoubled their efforts and managed to destroy the TIE bombers before they could release their payloads.<ref name="O" />

==Behind the scenes==
Pathogenic bombs first appeared in the [[roleplaying game]] adventure ''[[Omens]]'', which was published in ''[[The DarkStryder Campaign]]'' by [[West End Games]] in [[1995]].<ref name="O" />
